title: VendPoint Substitute Selections: Settling Period and Demand Pattern
content:
Rule of the VendPoint Industrial Vending Program on how the demand pattern of a Corbett-placed substitute's selection shapes the settling par recorded when the customer asks for a par change in the substitute's first three months.

**Rule.** The selection's demand pattern can replace the average per restock interval in the standard par, where the substitute's starter par is the par on its add entry and the largest single vend is the largest number of units of the substitute or of the retired item issued in one vend on the machine at any time: when fewer calendar days than the settling period have passed since the date of the substitute's add entry, the larger of two figures, the average per restock interval and the product of the starter par and the low-stock trigger fraction, replaces it; when the settling period has passed and the largest single vend is at least the average per restock interval, the larger of the average per restock interval and the largest single vend replaces it; otherwise the average per restock interval stands.

**Settling period.** 28 calendar days, counted from the date of the substitute's add entry to today.

**Trigger fraction.** The model's low-stock trigger percentage taken as a fraction of one hundred.

| Calendar days since the substitute's add entry | Largest single vend against the average | Figure in place of the average per restock interval |
|---|---|---|
| Fewer than 28 | any | The larger of the average and the starter par multiplied by the trigger fraction |
| 28 or more | At least the average | The larger of the average and the largest single vend |
| 28 or more | Below the average | The average per restock interval |

### Hypothetical cases (average per restock interval 2 units, 25% trigger)

- 27 days since the add entry, starter par 12: 12 multiplied by 0.25 is 3; the larger of 2 and 3 is 3.
- 28 days, largest single vend 4: 4 is at least 2; the larger is 4.
- 28 days, largest single vend 1: 2 stands.
